title: Hybrid ISTA: Unfolding ISTA With Convergence Guarantees Using Free-Form Deep Neural Networks

citations.claim: Zheng et al. proposed Hybrid ISTA, which incorporates free-form deep neural networks (DNNs with arbitrary feasible architectures) into ISTA-based unfolded algorithms while maintaining theoretical convergence guarantees.

Hybrid ISTA addresses a fundamental tension in algorithm unrolling: existing convergence-provable methods (LISTA-CP, LISTA-CPSS, ALISTA) restrict network architectures via partial weight coupling, while flexible methods (LISTA, ISTA-Net) lack convergence guarantees.

HCISTA integrates classical ISTA with free-form DNNs using a balancing parameter that controls the convex combination of the ISTA update and the DNN-refined update, ensuring convergence equivalent to ISTA in the worst case even with untrained DNNs.
HLISTA generalizes Hybrid ISTA to learned ISTA variants (LISTA-CP, LISTA-CPSS, ALISTA, Gated LISTA, ELISTA), enabling free-form DNN architectures while preserving linear convergence guarantees.
Zheng et al. proved that HCISTA converges under the Kurdyka-Lojasiewicz property, with convergence rates dependent on the KL exponent of the objective function.
Hybrid ISTA is the first framework to provide convergence-provable ISTA-based unfolded algorithms that support free-form DNN architectures without constraints.

Zheng et al. demonstrated that the hybrid ISTA framework can be viewed as a special ISTA-based connectivity structure that endows empirically constructed DNNs with theoretical interpretation and convergence guarantees.
In experiments on sparse recovery and compressive sensing, Hybrid ISTA models reduced reconstruction error with improved convergence rates compared to their non-hybrid counterparts.

do_not_claim: Hybrid ISTA was the first to unfold ISTA into a neural network
Hybrid ISTA eliminates the need for learned parameters entirely
Hybrid ISTA was applied to baseline correction or chromatography
Hybrid ISTA introduces the concept of algorithm unrolling
